blocks.text: Buenos Aires: aerial view of the Obelisk and city avenues

The sightseeing tour of the capital starts in the morning. See the Obelisk and walk through La Boca and San Telmo, with its cafés and restaurants. At Plaza Dorrego, you can browse antiques and see historic city houses.

Continue to Plaza de Mayo and Casa Rosada, the “Pink House,” associated with key moments in Argentine history and with Evita Perón. Your guide will explain how the city developed and introduce the neighborhoods and people that shaped modern Buenos Aires. In the old quarters, you can see how European architecture, port culture, immigrant traditions, and everyday South American life come together.
High-rise buildings by the water in Buenos Aires, Argentina
Buenos Aires: towers and their reflections along the waterfront

Breakfast at the hotel. Spend the day at your leisure or book one of these optional excursions.

**Tigre and the Northern Districts:** shared group excursion with an English-speaking guide, $100 per person.

**Fiesta Gaucha: a visit to Argentina’s gauchos**

Full-day shared group excursion with an English-speaking guide, $250 per person.

**Montevideo, the capital of Uruguay**

Full-day shared group excursion with an English-speaking guide, $400 per person.

A private excursion with an English-speaking guide is available for at least two participants at $650 per person.

Ferry tickets are included.
